suggestions.title: Press tomorrow: four honest sets or three — don't repeat Sunday's 8,8,7,4

rationale.science: On a cut you defend load rather than chase volume, and a working set is one taken near 1-3 reps in reserve. A fourth set that stops less than half way to the other three isn't extra stimulus — it's an extra slot on the scorecard that the session then fails (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021).
rationale.data: 8/6: press 250 x 8,8,7 drew PRESS - TARGET MET. 8/9: the identical top three plus a fourth set at 4 reps drew no press row at all, while rows, tricep, sulek and lateral each got one from that same session. Press still reads 4 sets on file and tomorrow is an upper day.
rationale.relationship: Chest went 3 to 4 sets on 8/7, so the target list re-keyed to four slots and the app's target check needs every slot met. A 4-rep fourth set fails the whole conjunction and the lift scores nothing, however good the top three were. The target list isn't saved with the session, so this mechanism is my best guess rather than a proven fact - but the observable isn't a guess: the best press in your record scored zero and the set count was the only thing that changed.

suggestions.predict: Run four sets with an honest fourth, or run three, and press draws a feed row tomorrow. Repeat 8,8,7,4 and it draws nothing again and 250 stays ungraded a second session. Withdrawal clause, restated: if you log four sets with a short fourth and press DOES produce a row, my reading is wrong and I'll retire it.

suggestions.title: The A/B your app started yesterday isn't on file — check for an arm before you train, and don't re-tap it

rationale.science: An A/B is worth its cost only because the assignment is recorded; that's the whole difference between it and just watching. Your own app says this about its Friday-vs-Tuesday comparison — without a controlled assignment it is 'a hint worth having, not a finding.' An unrecorded trial charges you the protocol and pays you no evidence.
rationale.data: The feed carries TRIAL STARTED - THE FAILURE A/B - TRICEP CAPPED vs SULEK ALL-OUT dated 8/11. The trials list in your synced state is empty.
rationale.relationship: A started trial is stored as { custom, started } with no id and no date. The sync merge keys trials on id or d and its union helper drops any record whose key comes back empty. So the trial dies at the first sync while the dated feed row survives - which is exactly the pair you're looking at. The decline path writes the same shape, so passing on it wouldn't stick either, and the guard that stops the proposal re-offering reads that same empty list.

suggestions.predict: Tomorrow's upper day prescribes no arm for tricep or sulek, and the same failure A/B can reappear in your inbox asking for consent again — re-tapping writes the identical unkeyable record. If tomorrow's protocol does name an arm for either lift, I've read this wrong and I'll withdraw it.
